title: The 150 Limit
hook: Everyone used to just know what was going on. Then the team grew and that stopped working.
statement: You can keep about 150 real relationships in your head. Past that, you need structure, not memory.
explainer: Below about 150, a group runs on trust and everyone roughly knowing everyone. Above it, those informal ties break and you need clear roles, written process, and smaller units.
sop: Count how many people each person has to coordinate with.
Compare that to the 150 Coordination Breakpoint.
Note where informal trust is already straining.
Add roles and written process before you cross it.
Split into smaller groups well under the limit.
equation_example: A team grows from 140 to 160 people. Under about 150, people know each other and sort things out informally. Past 150, those ties break and you need written roles and process. Smart companies split units before they hit it.
question: Count how many people your team works with regularly, and note how close you are to 150.
closing_statement: Know when trust needs structure to back it up.
caption:
Principle Nº 354: The 150 Limit

Everyone used to just know what was going on. Then the team grew and that stopped working.

You can keep about 150 real relationships in your head. Past that, you need structure, not memory.

Your turn: Count how many people your team works with regularly, and note how close you are to 150.
